messages:
zoe (docs): Hey team, small but confusing docs bug: the API ref for /v1/annotations/create shows the request body as an object with a single `items` object, but the live endpoint expects `items` to be an array. Example in the cURL snippet uses `{ items: { text: "x" } }` which 400s.

kevin (api): Yup, the schema changed during the v2 rollout from object->array to support multi-item uploads. Validator enforces array now. Old docs slipped through.

alan (sdk): Oof. The JS helper currently accepts either and normalizes to array, but our examples only show the object form. I'll update SDK examples and helper to prefer array and keep aliasing.

zoe (docs): Proposed fix: 1) Update the schema table to show `items: Array<AnnotationInput>` and an example array in curl/python/js. 2) Add a migration note: if you send a single object, wrap it in an array. 3) Add a short compatibility snippet for SDKs (helper that wraps non-array inputs). 4) Run linkcheck to ensure no old examples elsewhere.

maria (pm): Any customers broken? We should include a small blurb in release notes and the changelog for the breaking-behavior rollouts.

kevin (api): Most SDKs handled this already; only customers calling raw HTTP with the single-object shape saw errors after validator tighten. We'll call it a docs + migration note. No runtime change.

ci-bot: PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/957 by zoe (docs)  checks: lint, examples.

alan (sdk): PR includes updated docs/reference/annotations.md with array examples, updated examples/python/annotations_example.py, and SDK helper docstring updates. I also added a unit test that ensures the SDK wrapper converts object->array.

zoe (docs): Checklist before merge: update examples across guides, add migration note under "Breaking changes / Migration", ensure example JSON uses the canonical array shape, and add cross-link to SDK helper.

ci-bot: docs lint found two example formatting nits. alan (sdk) pushed fix.

ci-bot: All checks passed for PR #957.
